Slice: Register Neighbor

Intent

Let a neighbor join the tool shed by signing themselves up, so they can borrow tools. Signing up records the neighbor's name and the email address the shed uses to reach them. A new neighbor is active and can borrow straight away.

Trigger & Actor

A person who wants to join, from the Sign Up screen. They sign themselves up; the shed manager doesn't enroll neighbors. Someone whose earlier account is closed may sign up again here, as a new account. Once signed up, the neighbor signs in outside the model, and sign-in supplies their neighbor ID for every later action; it resolves a person to their newest account, or to their closed one only when they have no newer.

Command / Input

Command: Register Neighbor

A NeighborId is a UUID. Text fields have leading and trailing whitespace (any Unicode whitespace) removed; text that is empty after that counts as absent.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes A UUID chosen by the caller for the new account, so a retried request is recognised. Must not belong to a different account already registered (INV-REG-7).
name Text yes Trimmed. Must not then be empty (INV-REG-3), and at most 100 characters (INV-REG-10). Need not be unique (INV-REG-9).
email Text yes Trimmed. Must not then be empty (INV-REG-3), at most 254 characters (INV-REG-10), and shaped like an email address (INV-REG-11). Must not be held by another account under INV-REG-4, compared ignoring case. Kept as typed.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Sign Up @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Registered → context Neighbors Read by: Neighbors and My Account (their own slices, right after this one); and, for the neighbor's name and email, Tool Inventory (name only), Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Pickup Notices To Send, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors.

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command. Identifies the account everywhere from here on.
name Text yes From the command, trimmed.
email Text yes From the command, trimmed. The account's email until a later Neighbor Email Changed replaces it.
registeredAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. Shown as the sign-up date.

The event records a fact that never changes. A later email change is its own event; the name is never changed.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Neighbor Registered starts the new account's entry in two views, each specified in its own doc:

  • Neighbors (slices/neighbors.md) lists the new neighbor to the shed manager as active.
  • My Account (slices/my-account.md) shows the new neighbor their account.

Both are eventually consistent: the new account appears once each view has caught up with Neighbor Registered.

Invariants / Business Rules

A neighbor signs themselves up; the shed manager does not enroll neighbors. Every account starts active: Neighbor Registered is the only event that starts an account, and suspension and closure come later, from other slices. The Neighbors view shows a new account as active (INV-NBRS-2), and Check Out Tool lends to it under its usual rules.

  • INV-REG-3: Sign-up requires a name and an email address.
    • The shed emails neighbors, and only by email: overdue notices to borrowers and pickup notices to holders both go to this address.
    • A name or email that is empty, or only whitespace, is missing.
  • INV-REG-4: A sign-up is refused if its email belongs to an account that is not closed, or to a closed account that was suspended when it was closed.
    • An account's email is its current one: the email it registered with, or the latest Neighbor Email Changed for it. An email an account has changed away from belongs to no one.
    • Emails are compared ignoring case: Ana@Example.org and ana@example.org are the same address. The email is kept as typed.
    • Whether a closed account was suspended when it was closed is read from its Neighbor Account Closed (whileSuspended), never worked out from earlier suspensions and reinstatements.
    • One account per email. A closed account's email can be used again, so a neighbor who left can come back with the same address.
    • An account closed while suspended keeps its email for good, so a suspended neighbor can't get around the suspension by closing their account and signing up again with the same email. A suspended neighbor can't change their email (INV-CEM-3a, Change Email), so that email is the one they were suspended under.
    • A sign-up with a different email is accepted, even from someone whose earlier account was closed while suspended. Email is the only thing that identifies a neighbor. The shed manager sees both accounts on the Neighbors screen and can suspend the new one.
    • The same rule applies when a neighbor changes their email (INV-CEM-2, Change Email).
  • INV-REG-5: Signing up has no approval or verification step.
    • Neighbor Registered is recorded straight from the request. Nothing waits for the shed manager, and the email address isn't confirmed first. The new neighbor can borrow straight away, under Check Out Tool's usual rules.
  • INV-REG-6: A neighbor whose account is closed may sign up again, and doing so creates a new account.
    • The new account has its own neighbor ID. The closed account stays closed; it is never reopened.
  • INV-REG-7: Registering with a neighbor ID that is already used adds nothing new.
    • A repeat with the same name and email, compared after trimming, succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the account since. A repeat with different details is refused (neighbor-id-in-use).
  • INV-REG-8: Each account gets its own neighbor ID when it registers, and keeps it for good.
    • The neighbor ID is how every later event, view and command refers to the account. Names and emails are for people to read and for the shed to send email to.
  • INV-REG-9: Neighbor names need not be unique.
    • Two neighbors may both be called "Sam Lee". Accounts are told apart by neighbor ID, and only the email is checked for uniqueness.
  • INV-REG-10: A name is at most 100 characters, and an email at most 254, counted as user-visible characters after trimming.
    • A longer one is refused, never cut short.
  • INV-REG-11: An email must be shaped like an email address: an "@" with at least one character before it and at least one after it.
    • Nothing more is checked; the address isn't confirmed by sending to it (INV-REG-5).

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path (INV-REG-3, INV-REG-5, INV-REG-8)
    • Given: no account uses the email address ana@example.org
    • When: Ana signs up from the Sign Up screen as neighbor N1, with the name "Ana Ruiz" and ana@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, and the time it was recorded. Nothing waits for approval or email confirmation.
  • Whitespace is removed (INV-REG-3)
    • Given: no account uses ana@example.org
    • When: Ana signs up with the name " Ana Ruiz " and the email " ana@example.org "
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded with "Ana Ruiz" and ana@example.org.
  • No name (INV-REG-3)
    • Given: no account uses ana@example.org
    • When: someone tries to sign up with ana@example.org and a name that is empty, or only whitespace
    • Then: refused with name-missing: "Please enter your name." No event is recorded.
  • No email (INV-REG-3)
    • Given: the shed has no neighbors
    • When: someone tries to sign up as "Ana Ruiz" with an email that is empty, or only whitespace
    • Then: refused with email-missing: "Please enter your email address." No event is recorded.
  • Email used by an active account (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ana's active account N1 uses ana@example.org
    • When: someone tries to sign up as N2 with ana@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used to sign up." No event is recorded.
  • Email used by a suspended account (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ben's account N2 uses ben@example.org and is suspended
    • When: someone tries to sign up as N3 with ben@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used to sign up." No event is recorded.
  • Signing up again after closing (INV-REG-4, INV-REG-6, INV-REG-8)
    • Given: Ana's account N1, using ana@example.org, was closed while active
    • When: Ana signs up as N4 with "Ana Ruiz" and ana@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N4, a new account with its own neighbor ID. N1 keeps its neighbor ID and stays closed.
  • Email of an account closed while suspended (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ben's account N2, using ben@example.org, was closed while suspended
    • When: someone tries to sign up as N5 with ben@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used to sign up." No event is recorded.
  • Suspended, reinstated, then closed (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ben's account N2, using ben@example.org, was suspended, then reinstated, and then closed while active
    • When: Ben signs up as N9 with ben@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N9. N2's Neighbor Account Closed has whileSuspended no, so its email is free again.
  • Different email after closing while suspended (INV-REG-4, INV-REG-6)
    • Given: Ben's account N2, using ben@example.org, was closed while suspended
    • When: Ben signs up as N5 with ben.new@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N5, a new account with its own neighbor ID. N2 stays closed.
  • Email an account has changed away from (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ana's active account N1 registered with ana@oldmail.example and has since changed its email to ana@example.org
    • When: someone signs up as N6 with ana@oldmail.example
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N6. No account holds ana@oldmail.example any more.
  • Two neighbors with the same name (INV-REG-9)
    • Given: Sam Lee's account N7 uses sam@example.org
    • When: another person signs up as N8, also named "Sam Lee", with sam.lee@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N8. There are two accounts named "Sam Lee".
  • Email that differs only in capital letters (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ana's active account N1 uses ana@example.org
    • When: someone tries to sign up as N10 with Ana@Example.ORG
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used to sign up." No event is recorded.
  • Email kept as typed (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: no account uses ana@example.org in any case
    • When: Ana signs up as N1 with Ana@Example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded with Ana@Example.org.
  • Email not shaped like an address (INV-REG-11)
    • Given: the shed has no neighbors
    • When: someone tries to sign up as "Ana Ruiz" with ana.example.org
    • Then: refused with email-invalid: "Please enter a valid email address." No event is recorded.
  • Nothing before the "@" (INV-REG-11)
    • Given: the shed has no neighbors
    • When: someone tries to sign up with @example.org
    • Then: refused with email-invalid: "Please enter a valid email address." No event is recorded.
  • Longest name allowed (INV-REG-10)
    • Given: the shed has no neighbors
    • When: someone signs up with a name of exactly 100 characters
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded with that name.
  • Name too long (INV-REG-10)
    • Given: the shed has no neighbors
    • When: someone tries to sign up with a name of 101 characters
    • Then: refused with name-too-long: "Your name can be at most 100 characters." No event is recorded.
  • Email too long (INV-REG-10)
    • Given: the shed has no neighbors
    • When: someone tries to sign up with an email of 255 characters
    • Then: refused with email-too-long: "Your email address can be at most 254 characters." No event is recorded.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-REG-7)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org
    • When: the same Register Neighbor request for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • The same request after the account was closed (INV-REG-7)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, and N1 has since been closed
    • When: the same Register Neighbor request for N1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. N1 stays closed.
  • A neighbor ID reused for different details (INV-REG-7)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org
    • When: a Register Neighbor request arrives for N1 with "Ben Cole" and ben@example.org
    • Then: refused with neighbor-id-in-use: "That neighbor ID is already used by another account." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the person on the Sign Up screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. The neighbor ID is already used (INV-REG-7): a repeat with the same details succeeds with nothing recorded; otherwise neighbor-id-in-use.
  2. name-missing, then name-too-long (INV-REG-3, INV-REG-10).
  3. email-missing, then email-too-long, then email-invalid (INV-REG-3, INV-REG-10, INV-REG-11).
  4. email-in-use (INV-REG-4).
Reason Sentence Rule
name-missing Please enter your name. INV-REG-3
name-too-long Your name can be at most 100 characters. INV-REG-10
email-missing Please enter your email address. INV-REG-3
email-too-long Your email address can be at most 254 characters. INV-REG-10
email-invalid Please enter a valid email address. INV-REG-11
email-in-use That email address can't be used to sign up. INV-REG-4
neighbor-id-in-use That neighbor ID is already used by another account. INV-REG-7

email-in-use is the same for every case in INV-REG-4, with a sentence that is true in each, so a refused sign-up never reveals whether the other account is active, suspended, or closed while suspended.

neighbor-id-in-use can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen.

A missing or malformed neighbor ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: a repeated request with the same neighbor ID and the same name and email, compared after trimming and with the email compared ignoring case, succeeds and records nothing new, even if the account has since been suspended, closed, or had its email changed. So a retry after a lost response never creates a second account. The repeat is recognised by its neighbor ID, and is checked before the email rule, so it is never refused as email-in-use by its own earlier registration.

Two sign-ups with the same email at the same moment: the email check and the recording of Neighbor Registered happen as one step, so at most one is recorded. The other is refused with email-in-use.

There are no retries, compensations or external calls in this slice. No email is sent on sign-up.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: anyone may sign up; signing up needs no existing account or sign-in. Afterwards, sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the neighbor's ID for their own actions.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Registered holds the neighbor's name and email address. It is read by the shed manager's screens (Neighbors, Tool Inventory, Undelivered Notices, Flagged Neighbors, Suspended Neighbors), by the neighbor's own My Account, and by the two email to-do lists. No neighbor-facing screen shows another neighbor's name: the Tool Catalog never shows who has or holds a tool. Names and emails are kept with the shed's loan and hold history and never erased, including a closed account's; there is no erasure on request.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply INV-REG-4 and INV-REG-7, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (this slice): neighborId, name, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId, whileSuspended.
    • Neighbor Email Changed matches slices/change-email.md. Close Account is specified in a slice being written in depth; it is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Neighbors and My Account (a new entry); Tool Inventory, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Pickup Notices To Send, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors (the neighbor's name and email). Every later neighbor action (check out, hold, extend, return, change email, close account) and every shed-manager action on a neighbor refers to the account by its neighbor ID.

Open Questions

None.

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v1: v1 keeps the old view names in prose; the views named no longer exist in the model; deferred to v2 (2026-11-01, Mike Key)

Slice: Neighbors

Intent

Shows the shed manager every neighbor account that has signed up, with each account's current status (active, suspended or closed), on the Neighbors screen. It is the shed manager's one screen for neighbors: it shows who the system has flagged for repeated late returns and the late returns behind each flag, who is suspended and since when, and account closures, and it is the screen the shed manager suspends and reinstates neighbors from. The system flags; the shed manager decides.

Version 2 folds the former Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors views into this one: both were filters of the same accounts, and each offered one action this screen now offers.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the shed manager, opening the Neighbors screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per account ever registered, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. Nothing on this screen records anything by itself; its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Suspend (Suspend Neighbor slice) — offered on every active account, flagged or not (INV-NBRS-6).
    • Reinstate (Reinstate Neighbor slice) — offered on every suspended account (INV-NBRS-13).
  • Flagging is done by the system (Flag Neighbor). A neighbor is not told they were flagged, and a suspended neighbor is never flagged (Neighbors To Flag, INV-NTF-7). No email goes to the neighbor on suspension or reinstatement, and no reason or note is recorded with a suspension.
  • Showing only the flagged accounts, or only the suspended ones, is the screen's own filter over this one list; there is no separate read model for either.

Read Model / View

  • View: Neighbors built from events: "Neighbor Registered", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Neighbor Flagged", "Neighbor Suspended", "Neighbor Reinstated", "Neighbor Account Closed", and, to name the late returns behind a flag, "Tool Returned"
  • Consumed by: the Neighbors screen (Shed Manager)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. An entry reflects an event shortly after it is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Suspend and Reinstate check their own rules when they run, so a stale entry can't suspend someone who is no longer active or reinstate someone who is no longer suspended.

One row per account. NeighborId, LoanId and ToolId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded.

Field Type Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId Neighbor Registered.neighborId.
name Text Neighbor Registered.name. Never changes. Need not be unique.
email Text Neighbor Registered.email, replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed.email for this account. Always the account's current email.
registeredAt Instant Neighbor Registered.registeredAt. Shown as the sign-up date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone (INV-NBRS-5).
status Text One of active, suspended, closed. Derived: see the status rules below.
suspendedAt Instant Derived: suspendedAt of the Neighbor Suspended behind a suspended status; empty otherwise (INV-NBRS-12). Shown as the suspended date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.
flagCount Int Derived: the number of open flags on the account: Neighbor Flagged recorded since the account was last suspended, or ever if never suspended (INV-NBRS-10, INV-NBRS-11). 0 when the account is not flagged.
latestFlaggedAt Instant Derived: flaggedAt of the latest open flag; empty when flagCount is 0. Shown as a date in the shed's local time zone.
lateReturns LateReturn[] Derived: one item for each loan named by the account's open flags, as below; empty when flagCount is 0.
canSuspend Bool Derived: yes while status is active (INV-NBRS-6).
canReinstate Bool Derived: yes while status is suspended (INV-NBRS-13).

Each LateReturn item:

Field Type Source / Notes
loanId LoanId One of Neighbor Flagged.loanIds.
toolName Text Tool Returned.toolName for the loan.
dueDate Date Tool Returned.dueDate for the loan: the due date in force when it was returned.
returnedOn Date Tool Returned.returnedOn for the loan.
flaggedAt Instant flaggedAt of the Neighbor Flagged that named this loan.

To fill the late returns when a flag lands, the view also keeps, beyond its rows, each returned loan's tool name, due date and return date as Tool Returned carried them. These are bookkeeping, not rows, and are never returned (INV-NBRS-14).

Status rules. An account's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. closed — Neighbor Account Closed has been recorded for the account.
  2. suspended — otherwise, Neighbor Suspended has been recorded and no Neighbor Reinstated since.
  3. active — otherwise.

Flag rules. A flag is open from its Neighbor Flagged until the account is next suspended or closed; suspension and closure clear the account's open flags (INV-NBRS-11). A Neighbor Flagged recorded after a reinstatement starts the account's flags afresh.

Queries

  • List the neighbors. Takes nothing. Returns every account, each with every field above, including its late returns. There is no paging: the query always returns every account, ordered by name, then by registeredAt (INV-NBRS-8). The screen filters to flagged (flagCount above 0) or suspended accounts itself.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-NBRS-1: Every account appears on the Neighbors screen exactly once.
    • One entry per Neighbor Registered; nothing else creates an entry. A neighbor who signs up again after closing their account has a new account, so they appear twice: the closed entry and the new one.
  • INV-NBRS-2: Each account's status is active, suspended or closed, worked out by the status rules above.
    • Neighbor Registered → active. Neighbor Suspended → suspended. Neighbor Reinstated → active. Neighbor Account Closed → closed.
  • INV-NBRS-3: An account that is closed stays listed, shown as closed.
    • This screen is where the shed manager sees account closures. It is the record of every account; a closed account keeps its row, with no action offered and no open flags.
  • INV-NBRS-4: Closed is final.
    • A suspended neighbor who closes their account shows as closed, not suspended. No later event changes a closed account's status.
  • INV-NBRS-5: Each entry shows the account's name, its current email, its sign-up date, and its status.
    • The email is set by Neighbor Registered and replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed. The name never changes.
  • INV-NBRS-6: The screen offers Suspend on every active account, whether or not the neighbor has been flagged, and on no other.
    • Suspend Neighbor checks its own rules when it runs.
  • INV-NBRS-8: Accounts are listed by name, ignoring case, then by when they signed up.
    • So a neighbor who signed up again after closing appears twice, the older account first.
  • INV-NBRS-7: Applying the same event twice leaves the Neighbors screen as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-NBRS-9: Only the shed manager can read the Neighbors screen.
    • A signed-in caller without the shed-manager role is refused with not-shed-manager, and a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in. Nothing is returned to either.
  • INV-NBRS-10: A flagged account shows how many open flags it has, the date of the latest, and the late returns behind every open flag, each with the tool's name, its due date, the date it was returned, and the date of the flag that named it.
    • Neighbor Flagged names the late returns it uses up, as the loans they belong to. It carries no copies of names or dates. The view takes those from each loan's Tool Returned, which carries the tool's name, the due date in force at the return, and the return date.
    • Being flagged never suspends anyone by itself, and there is no dismiss action: a flag the shed manager decides not to act on stays open.
  • INV-NBRS-11: Suspending or closing the account clears its open flags; a flag recorded after a reinstatement starts the count afresh.
    • The flags were what the shed manager acted on, or can no longer act on. A suspended neighbor is never flagged (Neighbors To Flag), so no flag lands while suspended.
  • INV-NBRS-12: A suspended account shows when it was suspended; the date is cleared on reinstatement.
    • A suspension never lifts by itself after a set time, and it is never permanent. A neighbor suspended again after a reinstatement shows the new date.
  • INV-NBRS-13: The screen offers Reinstate on every suspended account, and on no other.
    • Reinstate Neighbor checks its own rules when it runs.
  • INV-NBRS-14: To name late returns, the view keeps every returned loan's tool name, due date and return date, whether or not the borrower is flagged; none of it is returned on its own.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana Ruiz registered with ana@example.org and Ben Ito with ben@example.org. Ana returned the ladder (L1, due 31 August) on 1 September, the drill (L2, due 15 September) on 20 September and the hedge trimmer (L3, due 1 October) on 5 October, all late.

  • Neighbor registered (INV-NBRS-1, INV-NBRS-2, INV-NBRS-5, INV-NBRS-6)
    • Given: no neighbors have signed up
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org
    • Then: the Neighbors screen lists Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org, signed up on today's date, as active, not flagged, with Suspend offered and Reinstate not offered.
  • Two neighbors with the same name (INV-NBRS-1)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for a different account, also named Ana Ruiz, with ana.r@example.net
    • Then: the Neighbors screen lists both, as separate entries.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-NBRS-7)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana once, as active
    • When: the same Neighbor Registered for Ana is applied again
    • Then: the Neighbors screen still lists Ana once.
  • Email changed (INV-NBRS-5)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana Ruiz with ana@example.org, as active
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for Ana, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: the Neighbors screen lists Ana Ruiz with ana.ruiz@example.net, still active.
  • Neighbor flagged (INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana as active, not flagged
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana on 5 October, naming L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as active, flagged once, latest on 5 October, with three late returns: the ladder (due 31 August, returned 1 September), the drill (due 15 September, returned 20 September) and the hedge trimmer (due 1 October, returned 5 October). Suspend is offered, as before.
  • Due date after an extension (INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: L2 was extended from 15 September to 18 September before it was returned on 20 September
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana, naming L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: the drill's late return shows due 18 September, returned 20 September.
  • Flagged again (INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana flagged once on 5 October, and she has since returned three more tools late (L4, L5, L6)
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana on 15 November, naming L4, L5 and L6
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana flagged twice, latest on 15 November, with all six late returns: L1, L2 and L3 flagged 5 October, and L4, L5 and L6 flagged 15 November.
  • Flag left alone (INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen has shown Ana flagged since 5 October, and the shed manager has not suspended her
    • When: a month passes with no Neighbor Suspended recorded for Ana
    • Then: Ana is still shown flagged once, with the same late returns.
  • Flagged neighbor changes their email (INV-NBRS-5, INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org, flagged once
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for Ana, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana Ruiz, ana.ruiz@example.net. Her flags are unchanged.
  • Neighbor suspended (INV-NBRS-2, INV-NBRS-6, INV-NBRS-11, INV-NBRS-12, INV-NBRS-13)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as active, flagged once, and Ben as active
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana on 7 October
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as suspended since 7 October, with no open flags, Suspend not offered and Reinstate offered. Ben is unchanged.
  • Suspended without a flag (INV-NBRS-6, INV-NBRS-12)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ben as active, not flagged
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ben on 9 October
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ben as suspended since 9 October, with Reinstate offered.
  • Neighbor reinstated (INV-NBRS-2, INV-NBRS-6, INV-NBRS-12, INV-NBRS-13)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as suspended since 7 October
    • When: Neighbor Reinstated is recorded for Ana
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as active again, with no suspended date, not flagged, with Suspend offered and Reinstate not offered.
  • Flagged again after reinstatement (INV-NBRS-11)
    • Given: Ana was flagged, then suspended, which cleared her flags, and later reinstated
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana on 20 January, naming L7, L8 and L9
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana flagged once, latest on 20 January, with only L7, L8 and L9.
  • Suspended again after reinstatement (INV-NBRS-12)
    • Given: Ana was suspended on 7 October and reinstated on 1 November
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana again on 3 February
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as suspended since 3 February.
  • Account closed (INV-NBRS-3, INV-NBRS-6, INV-NBRS-11)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana as active, flagged once
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ana
    • Then: the Neighbors screen still lists Ana, now shown as closed, with no open flags and neither Suspend nor Reinstate offered.
  • Suspended neighbor closes their account (INV-NBRS-4, INV-NBRS-13)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as suspended
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ana
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as closed, with Reinstate not offered.
  • Closed stays closed (INV-NBRS-4)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana's account as closed
    • When: an earlier Neighbor Suspended, Neighbor Reinstated or Neighbor Flagged for that account is applied again
    • Then: the account is still shown as closed, with no open flags.
  • Signing up again after closing (INV-NBRS-1, INV-NBRS-3)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana Ruiz's account, ana@example.org, as closed
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for a new account for Ana Ruiz, with ana@example.org
    • Then: the Neighbors screen lists two entries for Ana Ruiz with ana@example.org: the old account, still closed, and the new one, active, with Suspend offered.
  • Listing order (INV-NBRS-8)
    • Given: Ben Ito signed up on 2 October; Ana Ruiz signed up on 1 October, closed her account, and signed up again on 5 October
    • When: the shed manager lists the neighbors
    • Then: the accounts come back as: Ana Ruiz (signed up 1 October, closed), Ana Ruiz (signed up 5 October, active), then Ben Ito.
  • Listing the neighbors
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana (active, flagged once), Ben (suspended) and Cara (closed)
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists the neighbors
    • Then: all three are returned with all their fields, Ana's with her late returns, with no paging. Only Ana's entry offers Suspend; only Ben's offers Reinstate.
  • A neighbor tries to read the list (INV-NBRS-9)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen has entries
    • When: a neighbor, signed in without the shed-manager role, asks for the neighbors
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can see this screen." Nothing is returned.
  • No sign-in (INV-NBRS-9)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen has entries
    • When: a caller with no sign-in asks for the neighbors
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Read refusals: the list query refuses a caller without the shed-manager role with not-shed-manager ("Only the shed manager can see this screen."), and a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in ("Please sign in."). Nothing is returned on a refusal. These mean the same conditions as in the shed manager's commands.
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-NBRS-7). An event applied a second time leaves the entry as it was after the first.
  • Event for an account the view hasn't seen: events are applied in the order they were recorded, and every account starts with Neighbor Registered, so this can't happen.
  • Events on a closed account: a Neighbor Flagged, Neighbor Suspended or Neighbor Reinstated applied to a closed account changes nothing (INV-NBRS-4).
  • Stale actions: Suspend or Reinstate offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, on a neighbor who has just closed their account). Suspend Neighbor and Reinstate Neighbor check their own rules and refuse with their own reasons; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Neighbors screen is the shed manager's alone; neighbors see only their own account, on My Account. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role; only a caller with it may read this view.
  • PII & compliance: shows every account's name, current email, sign-up date, status, suspension date and late-return history to the shed manager, including closed accounts, which stay listed. A replaced email is not kept in the view. To name late returns, the view keeps every returned loan's tool name and dates, whether or not the borrower is flagged. Names and emails are kept with the shed's loan and hold history and are never erased.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, name, email, registeredAt.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Flagged (Flag Neighbor): neighborId, loanIds (LoanId[]), flaggedAt.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId, suspendedAt.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId, toolName, dueDate, returnedOn.
    • These keys match slices/register-neighbor.md, flag-neighbor.md, suspend-neighbor.md and the loan slices' docs.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Suspend Neighbor and Reinstate Neighbor.
  • Lineage: v2 merges Flagged Neighbors v1 and Suspended Neighbors v1 into this view (model reshape, 2026-11-01). Their docs stay in slices/ marked superseded by neighbors@v2.

Open Questions

None.
